messages:
jamie: Heads-up, saw a correlation between high egress util in rack-17 and 99th% latency spikes for shared GPUs. Noticed this right after onboarding a large tenant to a fractional dedicated slice.

oliver: Can you paste the metric query?

jamie: curl -s "https://telemetry.internal/api/query?m=egress_bytes_per_sec&rack=rack-17&window=5m" -> top src IPs show bursty streaming job from tenant 'vizco'.

rachel: That tenant's batch prefetcher was recently enabled in prod iirc. Could be aggressive connection reuse.

jamie: Right. When egress exceeds 800Mbps on that TOR we see NVLINK/PCIe stalls ripple to co-located GPUs 14 small tp spike -> slab evictions -> model tail latency climb.

ankur: Proposed mitigation: add an egress-threshold evacuation rule for slices. If TOR egress > 750Mbps for >30s, mark fractional slice as "soft-evacuate" and steer new allocs to fallback pool, leave existing jobs to finish with backpressure. Thoughts?

oliver: Sounds reasonable. Two concerns: 1) Evacuation churn causing cold KVCaches and higher token cost. 2) Cost shift to fallback pool (dedicated) 14 who eats it?

rachel: For 1) we can wire a KVC-winback TTL so small warmups persist through short evacuations. For 2) we should bill surge to tenant if it's above agreed egress threshold, otherwise company absorbs during rollout.

jamie: Implementation sketch: scheduler emits tor.egress metric -> routing service annotates slice -> allocator honors annotation and stops packing new fractional allocs into that rack. Also expose flag: infra.evacuate_on_egress=true for canary.

ankur: We should add a cooldown window 10m to avoid oscillation. Also gate by tenant priority: reserved/dedicated slices never get evacuated, only fractional & shared.

oliver: For canary, start in eu-west-1 on low-traffic racks. Add a probe that simulates a 3min burst to verify KV warmup cost and tail latency tradeoffs.

jamie: I'll put together runbook changes and a short script to annotate racks. Example drain step:
```
# mark slice soft-evacuate
POST /allocator/v1/slice/annotate {"slice":"slice-1234","annotation":"soft-evacuate:egress-750"}
# stop new packs to rack
kubectl label nodes rack-17 evacuate=true --overwrite
```

rachel: Make sure console shows cost shift estimate in rollout modal. Ops must see projected CPU/GPU token cost delta before enabling.

ankur: Also add an alert rule: if evacuation rate > 3 racks/hr, open an incident. That means systemic tenant behavior or config bug.

oliver: Agree. One more: include a temporary quota throttle as gentle alternative to evacuation 14 throttle tenant egress to 600Mbps for 2m before evacuate. Less churn.

jamie: Good idea. Sequence: throttle -> if continued violation -> soft-evacuate -> fallback routing. I'll draft PR for throttler + annotate hook.

sre-bot: [deploy-bot] rollout plan created: feature/egress-evacuate-canary -> staging -> eu-west-1 canary. Link: https://deploys.internal/rollouts/1212 :rocket:

oliver: OK, prioritize metrics around KV-cache miss rate, tail latency, and token cost during canary. Jamie, can you own the rollout doc? :thumbsup:

jamie: Yep, I'll write the doc and schedule a 30m sync after the canary run.

rachel: Assigning billing/pm to review surge charge policy.

ankur: I'll add the cooldown and throttle pre-check into the allocator.

jamie: Cool 14 will post status updates in this thread during the canary. :eyes:
